newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: PEACOCKS DONATED TO U.N. BY JAPANESE PARK.
newsitem.headline: PEACOCKS DONATED TO U.N. BY JAPANESE PARK.

text.p: Four female "bride" peacocks and one male, donated by a private park in Japan, are due in Geneva on Friday to repopulate the park surrounding the United Nations European headquarters, a U.N. statement said.
The birds will be quarantined in a cage for four weeks before being released on the sprawling grounds, where foxes have preyed on peacocks, leaving only three males.

"The birds come from the privately-owned Izu Natural History Park, which offered to donate them following a report in Japan's Asahi Shimbun newspaper that the peacock population of the Parc Ariana...was in decline," the U.N. statement said.
Peacocks freely roam the 25-hectare (62-acre) Parc Ariana surrounding the U.N. headquarters overlooking Lake Geneva. It was bequeathed to the city in 1890 by Gustave Revilliod who is buried there.

His will set conditions that the park, named for his mother, must be open to the public, his tomb must remain there and peacocks must be maintained on the property, covered with century-old cedar and cypress trees.
"The donation is being considered as an opportunity to mark the 40th anniversary of Japan's membership in the United Nations," the statement said.
